feat: Add /proc/net/route fallback for OpenWRT compatibility

Fixes #13

This patch adds a fallback mechanism to parse /proc/net/route directly
when the net_route crate returns None for the gateway field on OpenWRT.

The issue occurs because OpenWRT formats route entries differently
(using 'proto static src X.X.X.X' syntax), which breaks net_route's
parsing logic.

Changes:
- Add parse_proc_route_gateway() method (Linux-only)
- Parses hex-encoded gateway addresses from /proc/net/route
- Converts little-endian hex to IpAddr (e.g. 01F818AC -> 172.24.248.1)
- Falls back to this parser when net_route.gateway is None
- Logs warning when fallback is used

Benefits over NoOpRouteManager:
- Maintains automatic route management on OpenWRT
- No manual route configuration required
- Transparent operation on both standard Linux and OpenWRT
- Enables policy-based routing and split-tunneling

Tested on:
- Netgear WAX220 (OpenWRT 24.10, kernel 5.15, aarch64)
- Cross-compiled with 'cross' for aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
